comments.body:
(The previous one-word "placeholder" comment was an accidental post from a lock-availability
probe — disregard it; this is the real record.)

## Premise validated BEFORE implementing — and REFUTED

The gate is NOT blind to the attribute form. `_ScopeLinter._wrapper_name` in
`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` already has an `ast.Attribute` branch (`func.attr in
WRAPPER_NAMES`) alongside the `ast.Name` branch, and it has been there since the gate's first
commit, 6739ea54fa ("d37e: lint gates raw git writes to seams") — a `git log -S` on that branch
text returns that commit only.

### Escaping-example evidence (it does not escape)

Synthetic tree at `/tmp/rebar-4073-9d4f-c644-44a9/probe`, run via
`python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py --root <probe> --report`:

```
escape.py:2   [wrapper-git-mutation]      _git() passed mutation verb 'commit'  (UNMARKED)  # core._git(root, ["commit", ...])
escape.py:6   [wrapper-git-mutation]      run_git() passed mutation verb 'add'  (UNMARKED)  # mod.run_git(root, ["add", "-A"])
escape.py:10  [unresolvable-argv-wrapper] opaque argv forwarded to _git()       (UNMARKED)  # core._git(root, *argv)
escape.py:14  [wrapper-git-mutation]      _git() passed mutation verb 'commit'  (marked: probe marker)
escape.py:18  [wrapper-git-mutation]      _git() passed mutation verb 'commit'  (UNMARKED)  # bare _git(...)
```

`check` exits 1 on that tree. Attribute-form mutation verbs, attribute-form opaque-argv
fail-closed forwarding, a nested receiver (`core.sub._git(...)`) and `self._git(...)` all fire;
the `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker silences the attribute form exactly as it does the bare form.

### So why does `_ref_lock_push.py` have no hits?

Not the call SHAPE — the VERB. Its single wrapper call is
`core._git(repo_root, ["push", f"--force-with-lease=...", remote, refspec], ...)`
(`push_lease_cas`, line 116) and `push` is not in `MUTATION_VERBS`
(`{add, commit, rm, mv, reset, update-ref, checkout, clean}`). The gate SAW the call, resolved
its argv, and correctly declined to fire — so no marker is warranted there, and adding one would
be noise. That is AC2's first half.

AC2's second half is moot: there is no `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py` (nor any
`push_recovery` reference in `src/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/`), so
`cinderlike-lucky-akitainu` has not yet introduced those sites; when it does, the existing
attribute branch covers them.

### Considered and NOT done

Adding `push` to `MUTATION_VERBS` would make `_ref_lock_push.py` fire. That is a genuine but
DIFFERENT scope question — what "mutation" means for a gate whose stated policy is local store
writes (`git add/commit/rm`) — and it would flood every legitimate `git_adapter`/sync push site.
Recorded here rather than smuggled in under a detection-blind-spot premise.

### What remains real

Nothing pins the attribute-form behaviour: all 8 R2 tests in
`tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` use the bare `ast.Name` form. Untested, undocumented
coverage reads as absent — which is how this bug came to be filed, and a future refactor of
`_wrapper_name` could delete the branch with every test still green. The work is therefore AC3
plus documenting AC1's already-true answer, not a detection change.

## The gap AS FILED — refuted before implementing

`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` was reported to match wrapper calls only by bare callable
name, so that `core._git("commit", ...)` — an attribute on a module object passed in as a
parameter — would escape it. **That is not the case.**
`_ScopeLinter._wrapper_name` has carried an `ast.Attribute` branch (`func.attr in
WRAPPER_NAMES`) alongside the `ast.Name` branch since the gate's first commit, 6739ea54fa
("d37e: lint gates raw git writes to seams"), confirmed by
`git log -S'isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in WRAPPER_NAMES'`.

A synthetic probe (`/tmp/rebar-4073-9d4f-c644-44a9/probe`, `--report`) shows `core._git(root,
["commit", ...])`, `mod.run_git(root, ["add", "-A"])`, `core._git(root, *argv)`,
`core.sub._git(...)` and `self._git(...)` ALL firing, `check` exiting 1, and
`# raw-git-ok: <reason>` silencing the attribute form exactly as it silences the bare form.
Full evidence is in the ticket comment.

`_ref_lock_push.py` has no hits for a different reason: its one wrapper call
(`push_lease_cas`, line 116) passes `push`, which is not in `MUTATION_VERBS`
(`{add, commit, rm, mv, reset, update-ref, checkout, clean}`). The gate saw the call and
resolved its argv — it correctly declined to fire. `src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py` does not
exist yet anywhere in the tree.

## What is actually wrong

The BEHAVIOUR is right; the EVIDENCE for it is missing. All 8 R2 tests in
`tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` use the bare-name form
(`test_wrapper_literal_mutation_verb_fires` through
`test_sibling_wrapper_names_not_in_name_set`); not one exercises an attribute receiver, and the
module docstring says only "BY NAME". Untested, undocumented coverage is coverage that reads as
absent — which is how this bug came to be filed. Left alone it will be re-filed, and worse, a
future refactor of `_wrapper_name` can delete the branch with every test still green.

## Change

Two files, no detection-logic change (a detection change would be wrong — the detection is
correct):

1. `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` — a new R2 sub-section pinning the attribute form:
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_mutation_verb_fires` — `core._git(...)` / `core.run_git(...)`
     with a literal mutation verb each fire `wrapper-git-mutation`.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_receiver_shape_does_not_matter` — `self._git(...)`, a nested
     receiver `core.inner._git(...)`, and an imported-module receiver `_ref_lock._git(...)` all
     fire, proving the match is on the attribute and not on any particular receiver shape.
   - `test_wrapper_attribute_form_opaque_argv_fires_and_marker_silences` — `core._git(root,
     *args)` fires the fail-closed `unresolvable-argv-wrapper`, and the SAME line with
     `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` is clean. This is the ACs' "existing exemption mechanics must keep
     working" requirement, on the attribute form.
   - `test_attribute_form_push_lease_cas_shape_does_not_fire` — the real `push_lease_cas` argv
     shape plus an attribute-form read (`rev-parse`) stay clean, pinning the disposition so the
     absence of a marker on `_ref_lock_push.py` reads as resolved rather than as a blind spot.
2. `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — the module docstring's R2 bullet gains the explicit
   statement that the name comes from the CALLABLE, so an attribute call is matched by its
   attribute whatever the receiver, and names the late-binding `core`-passing idiom as the
   reason that matters. Docstring only; `_wrapper_name`, `MUTATION_VERBS`, `WRAPPER_NAMES`,
   `_check_wrapper_call` and every marker path are untouched.

## Deliberately NOT done

Adding `push` to `MUTATION_VERBS` would make `_ref_lock_push.py` fire. That is a real but
DIFFERENT question — what "mutation" means for a gate whose stated policy is local store writes
(`git add/commit/rm`) — and it would flood every legitimate `git_adapter` and sync push site.
Recorded in the ticket comment rather than smuggled in under a detection-blind-spot premise.

## Verification

- Mutation check (already run): deleting the two-line `ast.Attribute` branch from
  `_wrapper_name` turns exactly the three new detection tests RED (31 passed, 3 failed);
  restoring it returns 34 passed. The new tests therefore pin the branch rather than merely
  co-exist with it.
- Whole-repo re-run of the gate after the change: `python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py`
  exits 0 and `--report` yields the same 123-hit inventory as before, so no new hits need
  triage and no legitimate site needs a new marker (the change adds no detection).
- Full local gate set before push: every `scripts/check_*.py`, the generators' no-diff check,
  `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the CI pytest selection
  (`-m "not integration and not external" -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`), and
  `tests/integration` explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Attribute-form calls whose attribute is in `WRAPPER_NAMES` resolve: confirmed
      already true, with the reason and the probe evidence recorded on the ticket, and the
      coverage stated in the gate's own module docstring so it is no longer implicit.
- [ ] AC2 — `_ref_lock_push.py` is explicitly dispositioned (seen, argv resolved, correctly
      not fired because `push` is not a mutation verb; no marker warranted) and the
      `push_recovery.py` half is recorded as moot (the file does not exist).
- [ ] AC3 — Four tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` pin attribute-form detection,
      receiver-shape independence, fail-closed opaque forwarding, and marker sanctioning; three
      of them are shown to fail when the `ast.Attribute` branch is removed.
compiled_state.title: check_raw_git_writes misses attribute-form git wrapper calls
